title: Plant Biology
tagline: Plant cells and form, water and nutrient transport, photosynthesis, C4 and CAM, hormones, responses to the environment and reproduction
summary: Plants turn sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into the food and oxygen on which most other life depends. This course covers plant cells and tissues, growth and form, the movement of water and nutrients, photosynthesis and its variants, hormones and signalling, responses to light and stress, and flowering, fertilisation and seeds.

chapters.title: Plant cells and tissues
chapters.summary: Cell walls, plastids and vacuoles, and the tissue systems of the plant body.

chapters.title: Plant form and growth
chapters.summary: Meristems, primary and secondary growth, and the anatomy of roots, stems and leaves.

chapters.title: Water and transport
chapters.summary: Water potential, transpiration, the cohesion–tension theory and translocation in the phloem.

chapters.title: Mineral nutrition
chapters.summary: Essential elements, uptake by roots, mycorrhizae and nitrogen-fixing symbioses.

chapters.title: Photosynthesis
chapters.summary: Light harvesting, the two photosystems and photosynthetic electron transport, and the Calvin cycle.

chapters.title: C3, C4 and CAM photosynthesis
chapters.summary: Photorespiration, carbon-concentrating mechanisms and photosynthesis in hot, dry and shaded environments.

chapters.title: Plant hormones and signalling
chapters.summary: Auxin, cytokinins, gibberellins, abscisic acid and ethylene, and how their signals interact.

chapters.title: Responses to light and the environment
chapters.summary: Phototropism, phytochromes, photoperiodism and circadian clocks, and responses to drought, cold and pathogens.

chapters.title: Plant reproduction
chapters.summary: Flowers, pollination, double fertilisation, seeds and fruits, dispersal and germination.
